hash_convention: SHA-256 of committed normalized Git blobs; every tested working file matched its committed blob through repository filters.

environment.platform: Windows; isolated SQLite and loopback mock provider; existing local Chromium

python_batch.command: python -m unittest tests.integration.test_application_run_requests tests.integration.test_application_attempt_history tests.integration.test_worker_attempt_identity tests.integration.test_worker_lifecycle tests.integration.test_dead_letter_queue tests.integration.test_api_queue tests.browser.test_worker_attempt_recovery tests.browser.test_mock_run_controls -v

limitations: Local MOCK provider acceptance only; real ATS and external employer submission remain NOT_RUN/disabled.
No automatic takeover or fabricated completion of a RUNNING browser attempt; manual process-death confirmation/recovery for such a reservation remains a separate requirement.
PostgreSQL crash recovery skipped; these new scenarios use SQLite. No claim of new Redis or multi-host recovery acceptance.
Legacy API callers without request_id retain their original outbox identity and do not acquire the new frozen queue contract.
The existing Node v25.9.0 emits a Vitest supported-engine-range warning. Installed versions were not changed; tests and build actually passed.
implemented: Atomic caller-scoped run admission with frozen route/profile/document/supporting-selection metadata and mode.
Read-only scoped recovery of a lost acknowledgement; request reuse cannot change inputs or reopen terminal operations.
Stable worker operation ID passed into physical browser attempt identity, including retry/restart generations.
Current frozen inputs checked before adapter execution and again under physical admission lock.
Dead-letter retry, recovery and queue readback share unfinished-attempt and competing-operation fences.
Cancellation preserves immutable attempt evidence and never cancels through an ambiguous submission reservation.

observed_cases.observed: Test-owned worker exited 73 after its real Chromium attempt committed. Reopened database plus expired lease produced COMPLETED with operation attempt_count=2, exactly one physical attempt, review=1 and submit=0. Chromium relaunch was guarded to fail.
Real browser cancellation completed immutably with OPERATION_CANCELLED and zero provider review/submits; replay remained cancelled; a new reviewed intent completed with preserved old receipt.

Lost response left SUBMISSION_UNCONFIRMED and a dead-lettered worker. After database reopen, receipt-only API reconciliation confirmed the application; original attempt/operation history was retained and provider submit count stayed one.
Expired operation was BLOCKED, RUNNING browser receipt and PREPARED application preserved, and another browser intent refused.
Old dead letter remained terminal while the separately reviewed new request remained the only queued run.
